cards.headline: White's A18 is a blunder: the five-stone White group has only two liberties, so Black puts it in atari and captures it. S[DEAD], not S[ALIVE].

diagrams.caption: The tree's line. White 6 is the blunder, and the tree marks the leaf S[ALIVE]; the solver said DEAD.
Black 7 puts the five stones in atari. White 8 extends, but the group still has only one liberty, and Black 9 captures six stones.
If White 8 puts Black's stone at D18 in atari instead, Black 9 captures five stones first.

text: At the leaf, White 4 and the four stones joined to it have two liberties, at E18 and F19, and no eye space. None of the Black stones around them can be captured in time: Black 3 has two liberties, Black 5 is joined to the wall, and Black 1 to the stones on the H line. So Black 7 in Diagram 2 puts the group in atari, and White can neither escape nor capture first (Diagram 3).
Both reviewers agree, and the solver finds DEAD after every White reply to Black 7. White's corner stones, cut off by Black 3 and Black 5, cannot live on their own. The leaf is DEAD.
S[DEAD] is the right label, but on its own it makes the site accept Black 1 as correct. The two sections below say what to add to the tree, and why.

S[DEAD] alone is not enough: with it, the site would accept Black's G19 (see On the site, below). Keep the tree's answer to G19, White's B19, with the new S[DEAD] at the end of its line, and add White's stronger answer beside it: White 2 on the vital point. Any score under White 2 worse for Black than KO+ (S[KO-], S[KO-2] and so on, or S[ALIVE]) makes G19 wrong again; the exact score is not settled.

Diagrams 1 to 4 are the lines the grading check read under White 2, each with the S[] its reading supports. Black 3 at C17 needs no new line: besogo already finds that position in the tree's C17 branch, marked S[ALIVE]. Black 3 at B18, at C19 or at E19 stayed undecided; read those before choosing the score under White 2.
Do not fix the branch only by changing White's A18 at move 6 to D19, which leads into the main line's ko: G19 would then be as good as the main line, which this reading contradicts.

diagrams.caption: Add White 2 as a second answer to Black 1, beside the tree's B19, then Black 3 and White 4. Black gets a ko at best and falls short when neither side has ko threats: S[KO-] or worse on White 4.
Under the same White 2, add Black 3 and White 4. Black falls short when neither side has ko threats: S[KO-] or worse on White 4.
Under White 2, add Black 3 and White 4. Black falls short even with two ko threats more than White: probably S[ALIVE] on White 4.
Under White 2, add Black 3 and White 4. Black falls short when neither side has ko threats: S[KO-] or worse on White 4.

text: With S[DEAD] on the c117 leaf alone, the site marks a in Diagram 1 correct; today it is wrong. besogo also counts White 6 in Diagram 2 as a reply, because it reaches a position already in the tree: the main line after White 6 (Diagram 3), rated KO+. Once the leaf says DEAD, that is White's best move 6, so a scores KO+ instead of ALIVE, the same as b.

The grading check finds the new mark wrong, with moderate confidence. The tree answers a only with White 2 in Diagram 2. White's stronger answer is the vital point, White 2 in Diagram 4, which the tree already plays against Black's other wrong first moves. The solver could not settle Diagram 4 as a whole, so the check tested each Black reply against the main line's bar: Black must still win when neither side has ko threats. Every reply the solver decided falls short.

The solver treats everything outside its area as a Black wall, which only helps Black, so these failures hold on the real board. The three replies at z stayed undecided at up to 6M nodes, so this is not proven. A go player would expect it, though: in the main line Black takes the vital point and gets only a ko, so White taking it should be at least as good for White. So a is very probably worse than b and should stay wrong; the tree change above makes it wrong again.

diagrams.caption: Black to play. Today b is correct and a is wrong. With only the new S[DEAD], the site marks a correct too.
Black 1 at a, and White 6 in place of the tree's blunder. These are the stones of Diagram 3 after White 6, with Black to play.
The main line from b. Black 9 takes the ko, and the tree marks the leaf S[KO+].
White 2 on the vital point is White's stronger answer to Black 1. Black 3 at x lets White live outright; at y Black falls short when neither side has ko threats; z stayed undecided.
